title: Unusual experiences: the rain battle with Kid Rena, and Big Eye Louis
summary: He tells of playing second to Chris Kelly and a street battle with Kid Rena that Kelly won in the rain. Asked about Big Eye Louis, he recalls his alley cabaret and travelling with Keppard's band.

venues.name: alley cabaret behind St. Bernard Market

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Well, to sort of summarize this, or to end this, Herb, what were some of your most unusual experiences that you had in your career as a musician playing jazz? Well, I'll tell you,

when I came back from New York, Chris Kelly, I had a whole lot of music and I used to send him music. So, when I came back, they decided, at that time, they were starting to use two trumpets in the jazz band. So, Chris Kelly decided to use me. Well, I was playing second and most of the time, Chris Kelly would be having this fun walking around and talking with the ladies. Well, I'd be playing then. I'd let him play and I'd walk around. So, we had a ballet who were advertising one day and we happened to meet Rene. I think it was at Denver and Murray Street. At that time, Rene was in his full swing. Nobody could touch him in the Orleans, but one man, Chris Kelly. And that ace in the hole was the blues and the type of people, while we was playing that, they were crazy about the blues. So, it happened, we backed the trucks up back to back and we started to play and what happened? A shower of rain came down. And the band that would leave first would be declared the loser. That mean you run away. So, Chris said, he don't care if it's storm, he's not leaving. But the drummer, he passed his drums off the truck because he didn't want his hands to get wet and get ruined. So, we played in the rain and battled Kid Rene and Kid Rene left. And we all were soaking wet and we played in the rain. I'll never forget that accident. Tell us something about Big Eye Lord. He's known as Big Eye Lord. You call his full name, people wouldn't hardly know him. He used to play when I was a young man. He used to play in the alley, in the alley cabaret. That's right back of the St. Bernard Market on North Claiborne and St. Bernard's Treaty. That little cabaret was really red hot, red hot in those days. I guess that was around 1920 or before. Big Eye traveled with Freddie Keppett's Creole band for a while. Yeah, for a while.

Yeah. And he was also responsible for influencing quite a few of your clarinets, Bechet and musicians such as him. Yeah. He was a great clarinet man. He just about certainly don't recognize clarinet as a clarinet. Yeah, he was in the Orleans. Yeah. But he just have typified the Orleans, New Orleans jazz. Yeah, yeah. He's going when they say Big Eye Lord is
playing tonight. You can expect a big crowd.
